meetings.title: 4th Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: The agenda for this meeting is to elect the chair of the committee following the member change brought to the committee. At the start, this meeting was chaired by the deputy chair of the committee, MP Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim of West Maafannu Constituency. When the floor was opened, MP Asma Rasheed of Central Maafannu Constituency proposed, and MP Hussain Hameed of Kudahuvadhoo Constituency seconded the name of MP Ibrahim Shujau of Baarashu Constituency as the Chair of the committee. This proposal was unanimously passed by the members attended and voted. The voting details for this proposal are on “Votes” section of this page.

meetings.title: 2nd Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: In today’s meeting, the Committee met with the relevant officials from Teachers’ Association of the Maldives, Maldives Doctors Union and Maldivian Nurses Association. They conveyed their view on the Resolution that had been sent to the Committee. Additionally, they shared the challenges they face in delivering services in their respective fields.

meetings.title: 1st Meeting 2025
meetings.summary: The first item on the agenda for today's meeting was to elect the Chairperson and the Deputy Chairperson of the Committee. Director, Legal Affairs, Uza. Aishath Shifa facilitated the election of the Chairperson and the Deputy Chairperson of the Committee. Central Maafannu Constituency Member Asma Rasheed proposed to elect South Feydhoo Constituency Member Ibrahim Didi as the Committee’s chair. This was seconded by North Mahchangolhi Constituency Member Ibrahim Muhammad. The Committee unanimously decided to elect South Feydhoo Constituency Member Ibrahim Didi as the Chair of the Committee. The voting details for this proposal are on “Votes” section of this page. For the Deputy Chair of the Committee, Central Maafannu Constituency Member Asma Rasheed proposed, and Naifaru Constituency Member Yaaseen Abdulla seconded the name of West Maafannu Constituency Member Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim. The Committee unanimously decided to elect West Maafannu Constituency Member Mohamed Musthafa Ibrahim as the Chair of the Committee. The voting details for this proposal are on “Votes” section of this page. The Committee then decided on the working quorum of the Committee. Central Maafannu Constituency Member Asma Rasheed proposed 13 members as the working quorum, and Kudahuvadhoo Constituency Member Hussain Hameed seconded that proposal. This proposal was unanimously passed by the members present. The voting details for this proposal are on “Votes” section of this page. Next, the Committee decided on the voting quorum of the committee. Hoarafushi Constituency Member Ali Moosa proposed 12 members as the voting quorum, and this was seconded by Central Hulhumale Constituency Member Abdulla Shazeem. This proposal was passed with the majority of votes. The voting details for this proposal are on “Votes” section of this page. After that, the Committee proceeded to set a deadline for the resolution sent to the Committee. When the floor was opened to propose a deadline, Hoarafushi Constituency Member Ali Moosa proposed 23 July 2025. Central Maafannu Constituency Member Asma Rasheed proposed 30 July 2025. Neither of these proposals received support from any member. When Villingili Constituency Member Azim Abdul Azeez proposed 15 August 2025 as the deadline, it was seconded by Thoddoo Constituency Member Hussain Sameer. The Committee unanimously decided to set 15 August 2025 as the deadline for the resolution. The voting details for this proposal are on “Votes” section of this page. The final matter discussed at this meeting was regarding how to proceed with the resolution work sent to the committee. Accordingly, when Villingili Constituency Member Azim Abdul Azeez proposed to proceed with the resolution work in consultation with all relevant institutions, Thoddoo Constituency Member Hussain Sameer seconded the motion. This proposal was passed unanimously by the members present. The voting details for this proposal are on “Votes” section of this page. ﻿ Lastly, as no objections were raised by any members, the Committee Chair made the decision to give a 7-day period for public comments on the resolution.
